2.The proceedings were initiated under Tamil Nadu State Highways Act, 2001 for acquiring the petition mentioned lands.
The notification was issued on 12.12.2014 under Section 8 of the Act.
A portion of the lands proposed to be acquired had already been alienated by Thiru.P.N.K.Perumal in favour of A.Annadurai on 14.10.2009 vide registered sale deed.
Thiru.P.N.K.Perumal informed the authorities about the alienation already effected by him.
Yet, the purchaser / Annadurai was not associated during award enquiry.
An award came to be passed https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P(MD)Nos.25649 and 25654 of 2023 by treating P.N.K.Perumal as the exclusive owner of the entire property.
Interestingly, the award copy was not served on P.N.K.Perumal.
The entire award amount was duly credited.
Thereafter, when Annadurai raised issue that the land belonging to him cannot be taken unless he is paid compensation, the authorities realized their mistakes.
Now remedial steps are being taken.
It is at this stage, these writ petitions came to be filed.

3.The writ petitions are disposed of in the following manner:-
(a) The Award No.4 of 2022 dated 24.01.2022 passed by the fifth respondent is quashed as far as the petitioners are concerned.
(b) The fifth respondent shall pass fresh award after holding enquiry in respect of the writ petitioners.
The writ petitioners shall be entitled to putforth their case.
(c) Final award on merits and in accordance with law will be passed within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P(MD)Nos.25649 and 25654 of 2023
(d) Compensation amount shall also be disbursed accordingly to the petitioners herein.
The amount that has already been deposited can very well be withdrawn by the department.
(e) It is of course open to the petitioners to receive the award amount without prejudice to their claim to receive enhanced amount.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.
